subject: MLB salary cap
query: does mlb have a salary cap
title: Does MLB have a salary cap? No, but owners want one by 2028
answer: No. Major League Baseball has no salary cap, unlike the NFL, NBA and NHL. Teams can spend as much as they want on players. In November 2026, owners proposed a cap of $258.2 million and a floor of $180.2 million starting in 2028, and the players union calls a cap a non-starter.
body:
MLB said on Nov. 3, 2026, that it was proposing to phase in a salary cap and a payroll floor in 2028, Field Level Media reported. MLB said 12 clubs would have to add a combined $636 million in payroll to reach the floor, and eight clubs would have to cut a combined $528 million to get under the cap. Owners have also proposed limiting any one player to 15% of a team's payroll, the Associated Press reported.

The union opposes the idea. Interim executive director Bruce Meyer said caps "suffocate competition by offering owners an all-purpose excuse for inaction and mediocrity." The last time owners pushed for a cap, in 1994, it led to a 7 1/2-month strike and the first canceled World Series in 90 years, AP noted. The current labor deal was reached on day 99 of a lockout in 2022.

The five-year collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, 2026, at 10:59 p.m. CT, and a lockout is expected if there is no deal. Players instead want expanded free agency and arbitration, a nearly doubled minimum salary, more revenue sharing and a tax on teams with payrolls below a set level.
in_the_news: MLB owners have put a salary cap on the table in talks with the players union before the labor deal expires on Dec. 1, 2026.

faq.q: Why doesn't baseball have a salary cap?
faq.a: Players have long opposed one. The owners' last cap push, in 1994, led to a 7 1/2-month strike that canceled the World Series.

faq.q: What is MLB proposing for a salary cap?
faq.a: A $258.2 million cap and a $180.2 million floor, phased in for the 2028 season.

faq.q: Which MLB teams would be over the proposed cap?
faq.a: MLB listed the Red Sox, Cubs, Dodgers, Mets, Yankees, Phillies, Padres and Blue Jays as teams that would have to cut payroll.

faq.q: When does the MLB labor deal expire?
Will there be an MLB lockout?
faq.a: A lockout is expected if the league and the union don't reach a new deal by Dec. 1, 2026.
